If you count calories, you could budget in the drinking and not worry about these ups and downs you are having. For example lets say you need 2,500 calories a day to maintain weight. Your goal weight loss is 1 pound a week. 1 pound of fat is about 3,500 calories. 3,500 / 7 days (in a week) is 500 calories a day. You need a deficit of 500 calories a day to reach your goal of 1 pound of loss a week.

2,500 - 500 = 2,000 calories a day. That leaves 2,000 / 3 = 666 calories per meal (if you split them up perfectly, which i doubt you will do). The issue is you really want to drink. Lets say you drink 3 dark beers a night at about 150 calories each. 3x150 = 450 calories. We now need to subtract from your daily calories 2,000 - 450 = 1550. Thats 1550 / 3 = 516 calories per meal.

Lets say you start eating like this and you realize "self, i really want to eat more food each day - what do I do?". This is when you will switch up your booze for lower calorie versions. Lets say you switch to Vodka / Whiskey and use a 0 calorie or no mixer. Vodka is about 110 calories per serving. so 110x3 = 330. Your calories per meal has now gone up (2000 - (110x3)) / 3 = 556 (up from 516).

Even later you will start to think. "self, wtf. I really want more food - this booze crap is still so high calorie". You will then naturally start to drink less. 2 a night, 1 or maybe even zero. Getting your meal average back up to 666 calories.

All the while, you will be dropping nearly 1 pound per week, while still drinking (or not).
